long_biography.plain_text:
Freeman began in banking and business consulting before Granado's founding family asked him to find a buyer for their ageing Rio de Janeiro pharmacy company. Unable to attract one, he sold personal assets and borrowed from friends and banks to acquire the business himself. He preserved its formulas and archive while rebuilding production and distribution.

The revival gathered pace after Freeman acquired Phebo and developed stores inspired by historic Brazilian pharmacies. Working with his daughter Sissi, he combined vintage packaging with new products, broader retail distribution and European boutiques. A minority partnership with Puig supplied additional international reach without displacing Freeman's leadership, and he continues as Granado's owner-president.
